principle_hanging_text: Before you move, check that every piece is protected, and that the move doesn't remove a defender from something else.
principle_safety_text: Before every move, ask: what can my opponent capture, which checks do they have, and what does their last move threaten?
principle_free_material_text: When your opponent leaves a piece or pawn you can win, take it. Before every move, look at everything you can capture.
principle_forcing_moves_text: Checks, captures and threats force your opponent to respond. Before a quiet move, look at yours: one of them may win material.
principle_develop_title: Develop your knights and bishops first
principle_develop_text: In the opening, get your minor pieces off the back rank before starting an attack. Undeveloped pieces can't help.
principle_king_safety_text: Castle early and keep the pawns in front of your king where they are. Every pawn move there leaves holes your opponent can use.
principle_centre_text: Pieces and pawns that control d4, e4, d5 and e5 influence the whole board and make it easier to move pieces from one side to the other.
principle_activity_text: A piece with lots of squares is worth more than one that is stuck. Look for your worst piece and improve it.
principle_pawn_weaknesses_text: Isolated, doubled and backward pawns are hard to defend and give your opponent targets. Don't create them without a good reason.
principle_target_weaknesses_text: If you can force your opponent into isolated, doubled or backward pawns, they become long-term targets.
principle_passed_pawns_title: Passed pawns must be pushed (or stopped)
principle_passed_pawns_text: A pawn with no enemy pawns in front of it, or on the files next to it, can become a queen. Create your own and blockade theirs.
principle_outposts_text: A knight on a square that enemy pawns can never attack, defended by your own pawn, is often as strong as a rook.
principle_open_files_text: Rooks need open lines. Put them on files without your own pawns, where they can reach the enemy position.
principle_king_activity_title: Activate your king in the endgame
principle_king_activity_text: Once the queens are off, the king is no longer in danger and becomes a strong piece. Bring it towards the centre.

concept_hanging_piece_text: Before you move, check that every piece and pawn still has a defender. One left alone can simply be taken.
concept_count_attackers_text: A piece is only safe on a square with at least as many defenders as attackers. Count before you move there or capture there.
concept_free_material_text: When your opponent leaves a piece or pawn undefended, check whether you can simply take it before anything else.
concept_removed_own_defender_title: Check what your piece was guarding
concept_removed_own_defender_text: Before you move or trade a piece, ask what it was defending. Whatever it guarded can fall once it's gone.
concept_false_defender_title: Make sure a defender can really defend
concept_false_defender_text: A defender that is pinned, or busy guarding something else, can't recapture. Don't count it.
concept_greedy_grab_text: Taking a pawn costs a move. If it leaves your pieces behind or your king exposed, your opponent's activity can be worth more.
concept_fork_text: One piece attacking two at once wins one of them. Look for squares where an enemy knight, pawn or queen could hit two of your pieces, and use forks yourself.
concept_pin_text: A piece pinned to the king or queen can't move safely. Don't leave pieces lined up in front of more valuable ones, and attack pinned pieces again.
concept_skewer_text: When a valuable piece on a line is attacked and has to move, the piece behind it falls. Keep valuable pieces off open lines with something behind them.
concept_discovered_attack_text: Moving one piece can uncover an attack by the piece behind it. Check what each enemy move uncovers, and use the trick yourself.
concept_opened_line_title: Check which lines your move opens
concept_opened_line_text: Moving a piece or pawn can open a file, rank or diagonal for an enemy piece. Ask what can now reach your pieces or your king.
concept_trapped_piece_title: Give your pieces a way back
concept_trapped_piece_text: A piece with no safe squares can be attacked and won. Before sending a piece deep, check it can get back.
concept_in_between_move_text: Before recapturing or retreating, look for a capture or check first. Changing the order of moves can win material.
concept_remove_the_guard_text: If one piece guards something valuable, capture or chase that defender first, and what it guarded falls.
concept_missed_threat_title: Ask what their last move threatens
concept_missed_threat_text: Before every move, look at your opponent's checks, captures and threats. Answer a real threat before making your own plans.
concept_mate_threat_title: Keep your king safe from mate
concept_mate_threat_text: Check every forcing move your opponent has against your king, especially checks. A mating attack outweighs any material.
concept_back_rank_title: Give your king air on the back rank
concept_back_rank_text: A king shut in behind its own pawns can be mated by a rook or queen on the back rank. A pawn move such as h3 gives it a square.
concept_king_in_centre_title: Get your king out of the centre
concept_king_in_centre_text: Once lines open, a king left in the middle comes under attack. Castle early, before the centre opens.
concept_king_shelter_title: Keep the pawns in front of your king
concept_king_shelter_text: Pawn moves and trades near your king leave holes an attacker can use. Move those pawns only for a good reason.
concept_escape_square_text: A king with no free squares can be mated or checked again and again. Give it a flight square before trouble starts.
concept_perpetual_check_text: If a king can't escape endless checks, the game is a draw. When ahead, shelter your king first; when behind, look for checks.
concept_stalemate_text: If the side to move has no legal move and isn't in check, the game is a draw. When winning, leave the other king a move.
concept_attack_the_king_text: When the enemy king is uncastled or its pawns are broken, bring more pieces towards it and open lines.
concept_tempo_attack_text: A move that improves a piece while attacking something makes your opponent react. Avoid squares where your pieces can be attacked like that.
concept_lost_time_text: Every move should help. A piece that gets chased away or moved twice gives your opponent free moves.
concept_development_text: In the opening, bring out your knights and bishops and castle before pushing pawns on the sides.
concept_pawn_break_text: A pawn push that challenges an enemy pawn opens lines for your pieces. Prepare it, then play it at the right moment.
concept_passed_pawn_text: A pawn with no enemy pawn ahead of it or beside it can become a queen. Push your own, and block theirs with a piece.
concept_pawn_weakness_text: Isolated, doubled and backward pawns are hard to defend and give up squares. Create them only for a reason, and target your opponent's.
concept_centre_control_text: Pieces and pawns in the centre control the most squares. Contest it rather than letting your opponent own it.
concept_rook_activity_title: Put your rooks on open files
concept_rook_activity_text: Rooks belong on open files and on the seventh rank. Take open files first, and keep enemy rooks off your second rank.
concept_bad_placement_title: Put your pieces on good squares
concept_bad_placement_text: A piece on the edge, blocking another, or where pawns can chase it does little. Find each piece a safe, active square.
concept_key_square_text: Some squares matter more than others, such as an outpost no pawn can attack. Take them, or keep enemy pieces out of them.
concept_trade_decisions_text: Trade pieces when you're ahead or defending, and keep them when you're attacking. Think about which pieces are left afterwards.
concept_endgame_knowledge_text: In the endgame, bring your king into play, and learn which endings are won and which are drawn.
